newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels distribute food in east Zaire city of Goma.
newsitem.headline: Rebels distribute food in east Zaire city of Goma.

text.p: Tutsi rebels supervised on Thursday the orderly distribution of scarce food in the east Zaire city of Goma, scene of battles last week in which more than 400 people died.
The main commercial centre of Goma, capital of North Kivu province, is thoroughly looted. Thousands of smashed beer bottles line the streets.
Food stocks are low as many of the local food-growing areas are outside rebel control and in the hands of Rwandan Hutu fighters and Zairean soldiers.
About 1,000 people gathered on Thursday morning to receive hand-outs from a United Nations warehouse - oil, salt, biscuits and some maize.
Foreign officials of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees and other aid agencies fled Goma into neighbouring Rwanda last Saturday in a lull in street battles for the city and airport.
Shops and most hotels are ransacked. Rebels occasionally fire on groups of looters, but this has not deterred men, women and children from entering already looted shops, offices and homes.
In the city centre, a man emerged from one shop carrying two orange and white toilet brushes, long scrolls of computer paper and a harpoon gun.
Three children sat in a deflated rubber dinghy beside a half-completed building.
Goma was once a fashionable lakeside resort, in a region praised by guide books as one of the highlights of Central Africa -- an exotic mix of lakes, jungle and volcanoes.
Today it is practically on the front line of Africa's latest civil war.
Journalists heading west out of the city towards the front line with Rwandan Hutu fighters were able to travel more than than 10 km (six miles) before being stopped at rebel roadblocks.
It was impossible to glean any information about the state of refugee camps such as Mugunga, just a few kilometres (miles) beyond the roadblocks.

Mugunga camp, which last week became the world's largest camp with 400,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees, is the focus of worldwide concern. Rebels say there are many dead in the camps, from which aid agencies have been effectively barred for about two weeks.
The rebels, many of them ethnic Tutsis, have invited aid organisations to return to Goma but say they cannot protect aid workers if they try to reach refugees outside rebel-held areas.

"The front line is still in place. We are willing to allow NGOs and the U.N. to set up operating bases here, but we have no control over what is happening beyond our front lines," said rebel spokesman Hadisi Juma.
